test_title: SSC Selection Post HSC Level Official Paper (Held on: 4 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

His _________ violation of the moral code of conduct was too _________ to be forgiven.
solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **most appropriate** option to fill in the blanks is **2) flagrant; outrageous.**
 
• The **sentence indicates** that the person's violation of the moral code of conduct was severe and unacceptable.
 
• **Therefore,** we need to choose words **that convey** a sense of clear and obvious violation.
 
• **"Flagrant" **means clearly offensive or violating a moral or legal code, accurately conveying the severity of the violation.(उच्चाटनीय/उग्र)
 
• **"Outrageous" **means shockingly or extremely unacceptable, further emphasizing the severity and lack of forgiveness.(अत्याचारी/अतिदुर्भावनापूर्ण)

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *His **flagrant **violation of the moral code of conduct was too **outrageous** to be forgiven.* 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1) "fragrant; outgoing" **is incorrect. **"Fragrant" **means having a pleasant or sweet smell and does not fit the context of the sentence. **"Outgoing"** means friendly and sociable, which is unrelated to the violation of the moral code of conduct.
 
• **Option 3) "obscure; outstanding"** is incorrect. **"Obscure"** means not well-known or difficult to understand, which does not convey the severity of the violation. **"Outstanding"** means excellent or remarkable, which is not appropriate in this context.
 
• **Option 4) "magnificent; outlandish" **is incorrect. "Magnificent" means grand or impressive, which does not reflect the negative connotation of a violation. "Outlandish" means bizarre or unconventional, which is also not suitable in this context.

81:T75a,

The correct answer is "Option 3&
